steps.observation: You have 30 seconds. Write a short story about a lighthouse keeper.

steps.action:
Every night, Elias climbed the spiral stairs of Haverford Light, lantern in one hand, journal in the other. The sea below was a restless orchestra—waves crashing, gulls crying, wind humming through iron railings. When he reached the lantern room, he trimmed the massive wick, struck a match, and the great lens bloomed with gold, sweeping its reassurance across black water.

Years ago, a storm had taken Elias’s brother; since then, he measured time by rotations of the beam. At midnight, he opened his journal and wrote down every vessel the light revealed: “Midnight Star, outbound.” “Sea Finch, inbound.” He believed that naming them anchored them to life.

One fog-drowned dawn, Elias spotted an unfamiliar silhouette drifting, engine dead. He rang the warning bell until the air quivered, guiding the ship away from treacherous shoals. As it turned to safety, its horn answered in gratitude, and Elias, alone in the lantern glow, felt the silent echo of his brother’s thanks.
